technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Kafka features using Spring Integration Kafka module (spring-integration-kafka) as the primary integration point
Use Spring Boot auto-configuration for global defaults with @ConfigurationProperties for per-deployment overrides
Leverage Kafka Producer/Consumer configs for concurrency (consumer.group.id, max.poll.records) and compression (compression.type)
Implement ACK support using Spring Integration's AcknowledgmentCallback and Kafka's acknowledgment mechanism
Implement bindRequestor/bindReplier using Spring Integration's Messaging Gateway pattern with request-reply correlators
Implement batching using Kafka's batch listener (@KafkaListener with batch=true) and Spring Integration's aggregator pattern
For Sqoop integration, create a new Spring Integration Sqoop module or extend existing Spring Batch Sqoop support
Implement Sqoop job stop via Sqoop's Java API (SqoopTool) and process management
Capture Sqoop logs by redirecting stdout/stderr from Sqoop subprocess and piping to SLF4J/Logback
Implement incremental load using Sqoop's --incremental mode with last-value tracking in metadata store
All new features will follow Spring's coding conventions, include JavaDoc, and maintain backward compatibility
Tests will use Testcontainers for Kafka and embedded Sqoop/Hadoop for integration tests
assumptions: Development team has 2-3 developers experienced with Spring Framework, Spring Integration, Kafka, and Sqoop
Existing Spring Integration Kafka module codebase is available and familiar to the team
Sqoop integration is a new module; no existing Sqoop support in the codebase
Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.x baseline as per specification
CI infrastructure supports Testcontainers and Docker for integration testing
Documentation updates (reference guide, API docs) are included in estimates
No major refactoring of existing Kafka/Sqoop integration code is required beyond extension points
Performance testing and benchmarking are out of scope for this increment
Security hardening (SSL/SASL for Kafka, Kerberos for Sqoop) is handled by existing configuration
User stories U6-U8 (Sqoop) are related but separate from U1-U5 (Kafka); they share some infrastructure

activities.activity_description: Set up development environment, create feature branches, design documents for Kafka and Sqoop features, architecture review meetings

Implement global default configuration using @ConfigurationProperties (KafkaProperties), support per-deployment overrides via profiles/property sources, add concurrency (consumer concurrency, producer pool) and compression (snappy, gzip, lz4, zstd) options

Create comprehensive acceptance test suite for Kafka message bus using Testcontainers, cover producer/consumer scenarios, error handling, reconnection, integrate with CI pipeline (GitHub Actions/GitLab CI)
Implement manual acknowledgment mode for @KafkaListener, add AcknowledgmentCallback support in Spring Integration message handlers, ensure transactional consistency with Kafka transactions

Implement request-reply pattern: bindRequestor (gateway producer with reply correlation), bindReplier (consumer handling requests and sending async replies), use Kafka headers for correlationId, support timeout and error handling

Implement batch listener configuration, batch message converter, integration with Spring Integration Aggregator for custom batching, support for batch acknowledgment, error handling per record vs whole batch
Create new spring-integration-sqoop module, define SqoopConfigurationProperties, SqoopTemplate/SqoopOperations abstraction, dependency management for Sqoop/Hadoop libraries

Implement Sqoop job tracking and stop functionality via Sqoop Java API, process termination handling, resource cleanup (temp files, connections), integration with Spring's SmartLifecycle for graceful shutdown
Implement log capture by redirecting Sqoop subprocess stdout/stderr, stream to SLF4J/Logback with configurable log levels, support structured logging (JSON), correlation with job IDs

Implement incremental import modes (append, lastmodified), metadata store for last-value tracking (JDBC, file-based), integration with Spring Batch for orchestration, support for custom query incremental loads
End-to-end integration tests for all Kafka features together, Sqoop features together, and cross-feature scenarios, Testcontainers setup for Kafka, Hadoop, databases, CI pipeline integration
Unit tests for all new classes, mocking Kafka/Sqoop dependencies, target 80%+ code coverage, parameterized tests for configuration variations
Update reference documentation for all new features, create sample applications (Kafka concurrency/compression, request-reply, batching, Sqoop incremental load), JavaDoc for public APIs
Peer code reviews for all pull requests, address review feedback, refactor for consistency with Spring code style, performance optimization passes
Update changelog, version bump, release notes, compatibility matrix, publish artifacts to staging, smoke test released artifacts
